title: 6 Best Firebase Frontend Builders in 2026
summary: Six ways to put a frontend on Firebase data, from customer-facing app builders to internal tools for support and operations teams.
body_markdown:
Firebase gives you a database, auth and storage, but no frontend beyond the developer console. Customer-facing apps usually get built in code or with an app builder. The internal side, where support and operations teams look up users and fix records, is often left to the Firebase console, which gives everyone full access.


Below are six Firebase frontend builders, split by what they build, with the point where each one stops. For admin panels specifically, see the[Firebase admin panel guide](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/firebase-firestore-admin-panel) .


## The six options at a glance


Option Builds Code needed Cost


Jet Admin Internal tools and portals No Free plan; paid tiers


FlutterFlow Mobile and web apps Low Free tier; paid plans


Rowy Spreadsheet UI for Firestore Low Open source; paid cloud


Retool Developer internal tools Some JavaScript Free tier; paid per user


Appsmith Open-source internal tools Some JavaScript Free self-hosted; paid tiers


Custom React app Anything Yes Developer time


## Internal frontends


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin connects to Firebase and Firestore and builds internal tools on your collections: user lookup, record pages, forms, approval steps and dashboards. You describe the app and Jet generates it, then refine it visually or in code. Data stays in Firebase.


Support and operations staff get their own logins and only the collections and actions their role allows, instead of console access. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above; unlimited users are on every plan, including Free.


**Where it stops:** it is for internal tools and portals, not your consumer mobile app.


### 2. Rowy


Rowy gives Firestore a spreadsheet-like interface with cloud functions attached to columns.


**Where it stops:** it is a table view, not a multi-screen app.


### 3. Retool


Retool connects to Firestore and developers build internal tools with components and JavaScript.


**Where it stops:** developer-built, with per-user pricing.


### 4. Appsmith


Appsmith is an open-source internal tool builder with a Firestore connector.


**Where it stops:** JavaScript for most logic, and self-hosting is yours to run.


## Customer-facing frontends


### 5. FlutterFlow


FlutterFlow builds Flutter mobile and web apps with Firebase auth and Firestore built in.


**Where it stops:** it is for product apps; internal admin screens are extra work.


### 6. Custom React app


The Firebase JS SDK makes a custom frontend straightforward for a developer.


**Where it stops:** you build and maintain everything, including security rules for each screen.


## Which to use


- **Support or ops teams need Firebase data without console access:** Jet Admin.
- **You want a spreadsheet view on Firestore:** Rowy.
- **Developers will build internal tools:** Retool or Appsmith.
- **You are building the customer app:** FlutterFlow or custom code.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is the Firebase console enough for internal teams?


Rarely. Console access gives project-level permissions, so a support agent who can view users can often change or delete data too.


### Does a frontend builder bypass Firestore security rules?


Tools that connect with a service account do, so access control has to live in the tool. That is why roles in the frontend matter.


## Stop sharing the console


[Connect Firebase to Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/integrations/firebase) and give each team its own frontend.
